transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can’t seem to settle anymore. It feels like I’m restless inside my own skin, like I have to get up and do the next thing even when I’m worn out and should be able to sit still.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts or urges to perform specific rituals?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t have rituals I feel I have to do, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?
I’m not sure I’d say anxious most of the time. I do get worked up sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it as anxiety all day or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having trouble staying seated when you're supposed to be still?

Yes, very often. Even at church meetings, I’m tapping my foot or rubbing the edge of my purse, and I keep shifting around in the chair. Sometimes the ladies next to me start looking over, so I know they notice it too.
Do you often act on impulse without fully thinking things through?
Yes, I do. I’ll interrupt people more than I mean to, especially in committee meetings. A thought pops into my head and I just blurt it out before I lose it, even if someone else is still talking.
Do you often feel worried about the future or things that might happen?
I don’t think I worry about the future all that much. I mean, I have normal concerns like anyone, but it’s not something I’m sitting around thinking about all the time.
Did you have trouble sitting still or behaving impulsively when you were a child?

Yes, I did. Even back in grade school, my teachers would say I was bright, but careless. I was always losing papers, talking when I wasn’t supposed to, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Yes, I do. I make little mistakes that end up causing a lot of trouble. Like I’ll write the wrong amount in the garden checkbook, or I’ll leave someone’s name off the church supper list even though I really thought I checked it. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be careless, but it keeps happening.
Do you have trouble sitting still or feel restless at work or when you're at home, not just in formal settings like church?

Yes. It’s not just in church or places like that. Even at home, I feel like I can’t settle down inside my own skin. I’ll be worn out and know I should sit, but I feel like I have to get up and do the next thing. It’s a restless feeling, like I can’t just be still.
Do you have intense emotional reactions to situations that might not seem to warrant such a strong response?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I can get upset like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed that my reactions are especially intense or out of proportion. Could you maybe say what kind of situations you mean?
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Yes, very much so. If I’m sitting at the kitchen table trying to sort bills or paperwork, it doesn’t take much. A car door outside, my phone lighting up, or even just remembering something about the garden can pull me completely away from what I was doing. Then I lose my place and have to start over.
Have you experienced these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity your whole life, or did they start at some point as you got older?

It’s been there as far back as I can remember. Even in grade school, my teachers would write that I was bright but careless. I was always losing papers, talking when I wasn’t supposed to, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work. So no, it didn’t just start when I got older.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and impulsivity in all areas of your life, including work, home, and social situations?

Yes, it shows up pretty much everywhere. At home, my family has had to step in and help with bills and paperwork because I get off track or don’t follow through. And with things at church or in the garden, I’ve dropped responsibilities or forgotten parts of plans, and other people had to redo things or cover for me.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. These are groups I care about, and I can tell people don’t feel like they can really count on me the way they used to.
